claims.text: The starting material is a Ti–Ni high-entropy alloy in a homogenized, single-phase solid-solution state.
The starting alloy can be produced in the stated condition by conventional processing.
A 30–50% cold-rolling thickness reduction is an appropriate intervention range for promoting nano-twinning in this alloy.
Annealing slightly below 600°C for approximately 15–30 minutes in an inert atmosphere can retain deformation-induced nano-twins.
The proposed shortened annealing treatment can avoid full recrystallization.
The proposed processing can preserve the single-phase solid-solution state.
The intervention will produce a high density of nano-scale twin boundaries distributed uniformly through the microstructure.
The nano-scale twin boundaries will remain stable during elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing.
Nano-twin boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Dislocation blocking by nano-twin boundaries increases work hardening.
Nano-twinning will retain both strength and ductility at elevated temperature.
The treated alloy will have greater elevated-temperature yield strength than the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will have improved strain hardening under elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing.
The treated alloy will have greater creep resistance than the untreated baseline.
The expected benefits apply to Ti–Ni high-entropy alloys that remain single-phase solid solutions during high-temperature or extreme-environment testing.

contradictions.description: The treated material is defined as beginning in a homogenized single-phase state, whereas the baseline may be either conventionally processed or as-cast. An as-cast control may differ in homogenization, segregation, grain structure, and phase state, so it is not necessarily the same material without only the nano-twinning intervention.
